chapter: Instruments, tenors and the current band
title: The Steely Dan material and Victor Feldman's arrangement
summary: A band pianist introduced Steely Dan; Dick LaPalm assigned the arrangements to former writers Broadbent, Stapleton and Victor Feldman.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Uh-huh. Then the other side of the album has some things that -- composers you haven't --

I was not aware until the guys in the band started to play tapes for me, where I could be present and I think that one of the people in the band who'd made it very evident to me and even transcribed the words so I'd know what the lyrics were about, because very often, with my bad hearing and my lack of perception, I wasn't able to dig all the taped words.
You're talking about Steely Dan.

Steely Dan, right. And I think Pat Coyle, the pianist of in that season, said, Man, these changes are beautiful and we're going to dig all this within, so I sat and listened with him, as he transcribed the lyrics to me and the whole thing. And I said, "Yeah, that's really quite lovely." And I got back to -- well, actually I hadn't heard Vinandi-
yet then play them from Dick La Palm, but when I did, I said, 'Yeah, I'm aware of the pieces and I think it's a good idea.' Because it was basically Dick's idea to do the Steely Dan thing.
Then you divided the assignments to a number of writers to contribute.
Yeah. Well, Dick did that.
Dick did that?
Yeah.
I see.

Yeah, he picked two people -- two or three which had been former writers of mine, but he felt that they were in a position to cope with these pieces and so on, and they would be -- for instance, just to give you, like, the people that I think that made the biggest impact, that had been able to put the idea together, they had to be Alan Broadbent, it had to be Bill Stapleton and I think the whole pivot was on a guy by the name of Victor Feldman because he was in my band 20 years ago.
Uh-huh.
And he's been closer to the scene out here in pop music and everything else, than I had been. He certainly would understand what I was trying for.
I see.
And in the middle of I Got the News, ("String of Pearls" -- ed.) when he said (singing), I knew that he knew exactly where I was.
Oh, that's great.
You know, it's this whole telltale thing that you can tell about each other. Our humor was still the same.
Uh-huh. So it was a long gap between association, wasn't it?
Oh, yeah, yeah.
Yeah, I was very surprised.
As a matter of fact, Victor was in -- I think last in a Las Vegas group I had.
Uh-huh.
Where he had to double between drums and vibraphone.
Who thought of Victor Feldman? Dick also?
Of course. Because Victor Feldman was into the whole scene and that's been -- as a matter of fact he's been into all the Steely Dan sides since they began.
So it was logical.
It may be logical --
You couldn't find a better fit.
Right.
